en: During a thunderstorm, avoid standing under tall, isolated trees because lightning is most likely to strike the highest object.
Washing your hands after playing in soil prevents infections from harmful bacteria like Clostridium tetani, which causes tetanus.
Inhaling fine dust from cutting quartz rocks can damage your lungs, so miners must wear protective masks.
Stagnant water in uncovered containers after heavy rain breeds Aedes aegypti mosquitoes, which transmit dengue fever.
Looking directly at the Sun without special eclipse glasses can permanently damage your retinas and cause blindness.
If you get lost at night, you can find true north by locating the bright North Star.
The Moon's gravity causes high tides that create dangerous rip currents, so always check tide schedules before swimming.
During an earthquake, dropping to the ground and taking cover under a sturdy desk protects you from falling debris.
Wearing an N95 mask during Mayon Volcano's ashfall prevents fine, abrasive ash particles from irritating your lungs.
Wearing rubber boots during typhoon floods protects you from leptospirosis, a severe infection spread by rat urine in floodwaters.
Drinking plenty of water when the heat index is high prevents heatstroke, a dangerous condition where your body overheats.
You can still get sunburned on cloudy days because up to eighty percent of the Sun's ultraviolet rays pass through clouds.
